population: Unselected mild-to-moderate AD (clinical diagnosis, no biomarker selection)
note: Three selective H3 antagonists were procognitive across the standard rodent memory battery and were dosed to rodent-derived exposure targets, yet none moved the primary cognitive endpoint in unselected mild-to-moderate AD; human PET later showed the preclinical systems under-called GSK239512's affinity about 9-fold.
label: Alzheimer's (H3 antagonists)

engagement.model: Rat ex-vivo H3 receptor occupancy tied to procognitive doses (ABT-288)
engagement.note: ABT-288 occupancy in rat brain was related to the doses and exposures active in rat behavioural tests; no human occupancy study was ever run.
engagement.short: Rat occupancy set the target; no human PET
engagement.quote: In vivo rat brain H(3)R occupancy of ABT-288 was assessed in relation to rodent doses and exposure levels in behavioral tests.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level (JPET full text paywalled); the absence of a human occupancy study is stated in Othman 2013 (PMC3635600).
engagement.judgement: Opens the cell at the first published use of the rat occupancy system for a member drug. Othman 2013 states 'A receptor occupancy study in humans was not conducted for ABT-288'; the 25-70 % occupancy quoted for the phase 2 doses was calculated from in-vitro Ki, never measured, so the rat occupancy model has no patient comparison and stays untested. The GSK239512 PET system is a different model with a different prediction and gets its own track.
engagement.population: Unselected mild-to-moderate AD (clinical diagnosis, no biomarker selection)

engagement.model: Pig PET and in-vitro H3 affinity of GSK239512 (vs human [11C]GSK189254 PET)
engagement.note: Human PET found 62-97 % H3 occupancy at 6-120 ug single doses; in-vivo affinity was ~9x the pig PET estimate and >10x in vitro.
engagement.short: Occupancy reached; pig PET under-called affinity 9x
engagement.quote: The affinity of GSK239512 for brain H3 receptors in humans in vivo is much higher than that expected from studies in vitro, and higher than that observed in PET studies in pigs.
engagement.confidence_note: Seven healthy male volunteers, single oral doses of 6, 14 or 120 ug; pig PET data are cited as unpublished. Full text read (PMC3952801). No NCT number found for the PET study; registry lookup not possible.
engagement.judgement: Separate track from the ABT-288 rat system (different model, different prediction). Scored same because the readout the preclinical system used (H3 occupancy) moved in dosed humans, at every dose down to 6 ug. Magnitude off_by_>5x on the in-vivo KD: human 4.50e-12 M vs pig PET 3.98e-11 M (8.8x) and in vitro 1.26-2.00e-10 M (28-44x); source_calls_it scaling because the authors say dose selection without the human PET 'would be erroneously high'. The AD phase 2 doses (10-80 ug, Grove 2014) sit above the 6 ug dose that already gave 62-70 % occupancy.
engagement.magnitude_basis: in-vivo KD for 50 % H3 occupancy: human 4.50e-12 M vs pig PET 3.98e-11 M and in vitro 1.26-2.00e-10 M
engagement.population: Unselected mild-to-moderate AD (clinical diagnosis, no biomarker selection)

dose.model: Rat five-trial inhibitory avoidance (SHR pups) exposure-response (ABT-288)
dose.note: ABT-288 plasma 0.1-2 ng/mL (~10-40 % occupancy) was procognitive in rat pups; this exposure band became the human target.
dose.quote: In rat behavioral tests, ABT-288 improved acquisition of a five-trial inhibitory avoidance test in rat pups (0.001-0.03 mg/kg), social recognition memory in adult rats (0.03-0.1 mg/kg), and spatial learning and reference memory in a rat water maze test (0.1-1.0 mg/kg).
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level; the 0.1-2 ng/mL efficacious plasma band and its ~10-40 % occupancy are quoted from Othman 2013, which cites this paper.
dose.judgement: Opener for the rat exposure-response track. SAR110894 (0.5-5 mg) and GSK239512 (10-80 ug) carry no published rodent exposure target that I could compare, so this track is ABT-288's.
dose.population: Unselected mild-to-moderate AD (clinical diagnosis, no biomarker selection)

dose.model: Rat five-trial inhibitory avoidance (SHR pups) exposure-response (ABT-288)
dose.note: Healthy volunteers reached and exceeded the rat band at the tolerated 3 mg (steady-state Cmax ~5 ng/mL); sleep AEs capped dosing only at 5-6 mg.
dose.short: Rat exposure reached and tolerated at 3 mg
dose.quote: The 1 mg once-daily dose was selected in order to examine the possibility of achieving efficacy with low levels of receptor occupancy as suggested by the SHR pup Five-Trial Inhibitory Avoidance model.
dose.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC3635600). Wiley online-first date not verified; Europe PMC lists first publication 2013-05-01, so year is the print year.
dose.judgement: Decision 16: Esbenshade 2012 stated a wide CNS safety margin and rat EEG put wake-promoting exposures above procognitive ones; in humans the dose-limiting insomnia/abnormal dreams appeared at 5-6 mg, while 3 mg (Cmax ~5 ng/mL, ~2.5x the top of the 0.1-2 ng/mL rat band; predicted 50-70 % occupancy) was tolerated, so the margin held and the target was reached without that toxicity: same, margin_stated true. Magnitude within_2x on plasma concentration (1 mg steady state ~1.7 ng/mL sits inside the rat band). No human occupancy was measured; the occupancy figures are in-vitro-Ki projections.
dose.magnitude_basis: steady-state plasma concentration at 1-3 mg vs the rat-efficacious 0.1-2 ng/mL band
dose.population: Unselected mild-to-moderate AD (clinical diagnosis, no biomarker selection)

efficacy.model: Rodent procognitive battery (rat inhibitory avoidance, social recognition, water maze; rat/mouse object recognition with scopolamine or Abeta25-35 deficits)
efficacy.note: ABT-288 and SAR110894 were procognitive across rat and mouse memory tests, including scopolamine and Abeta25-35 deficit models; GSK239512 rode on sibling GSK189254 data.
efficacy.short: Procognitive in rat and mouse memory tests
efficacy.quote: Thus, ABT-288 is a selective H(3)R antagonist with broad procognitive efficacy in rodents and excellent drug-like properties that support its advancement to the clinical area.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level for Esbenshade 2012 and Griebel 2012 (https://doi.org/10.1016/j.pbb.2012.04.004, SAR110894, epub 2012-04-21); Medhurst 2007 (https://doi.org/10.1124/jpet.107.120311) is the GSK189254 sibling paper.
efficacy.judgement: One track for the three sponsors' rodent cognition batteries: same model type, same prediction (symptomatic cognitive benefit). Member first use is 2012 (Griebel April, Esbenshade July); Medhurst 2007 used GSK189254, a non-member sibling, so it does not open the strip.
efficacy.population: Unselected mild-to-moderate AD (clinical diagnosis, no biomarker selection)

efficacy.model: Rodent procognitive battery (GSK189254 sibling data for GSK239512)
efficacy.note: GSK239512 10-80 ug hit one co-primary (CogState episodic memory, ES 0.35, p=0.0495) but not executive/working memory or ADAS-Cog in 196 untreated AD patients.
efficacy.quote: Compared to placebo, GSK239512 improved Episodic Memory at Week 16 (Effect Size [ES] =0.35; p=0.0495). No statistically significant differences were observed on other cognitive domains or on clinical measures including the Alzheimer's Disease Assessment Scale-Cognitive Subscale (ADASCog).
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Bentham paywall). Online date 2013-12-12 is read from the Bentham DOI timestamp, print 2014. NCT01009255 has no posted results. GSK's own rodent data on GSK239512 are not published; the model side is the sibling GSK189254 paper, so product_in_model is false.
efficacy.judgement: Co-primary design: one endpoint met at p=0.0495, the other and ADAS-Cog did not, and GSK did not take the drug further in AD. By the v3 rule partial agreement is same with source_calls_it partial; I would call this a failure by the usual co-primary convention and say so here, but the status follows the rule. Nathan 2013 phase 1b (https://doi.org/10.2174/1567205011310030003) reported larger effect sizes (0.56-1.37) in 24 patients that did not hold.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: CogState episodic memory composite effect size 0.35 vs placebo; executive/working memory co-primary and ADAS-Cog null
efficacy.population: Unselected mild-to-moderate AD (clinical diagnosis, no biomarker selection)

patient_trials.quote: Co-primary efficacy endpoints were change from baseline in Episodic Memory and Executive Function/Working Memory composite scores from the CogState neuropsychological test battery (NTB) at Week 16.

efficacy.model: Rodent procognitive battery (ABT-288 in rat inhibitory avoidance, social recognition, water maze)
efficacy.note: ABT-288 1 and 3 mg were numerically worse than placebo on ADAS-Cog13 in 242 patients; stopped for futility while donepezil worked.
efficacy.quote: ABT-288 did not demonstrate efficacy in the symptomatic treatment of Alzheimer's dementia.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Sage full text returned 403); the abstract itself sets the preclinical efficacy and the failed trial side by side. NCT01018875 has no posted results.
efficacy.judgement: Comparison stated: the same abstract records 'efficacy across several preclinical cognitive domains' and 'did not demonstrate efficacy'. Magnitude opposite because the ADAS-Cog point estimates sat on the wrong side of placebo (not significant). The positive-control donepezil arm worked, so the trial could detect a symptomatic effect. The parallel ABT-288 schizophrenia failure (Haig 2014, Schizophr Bull) is another indication and is not scored.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: ADAS-Cog13 change vs placebo, both doses numerically inferior to placebo (not significant), futility stop
efficacy.population: Unselected mild-to-moderate AD (clinical diagnosis, no biomarker selection)

patient_trials.quote: The study was prematurely terminated because futility criteria were met.

efficacy.model: Rodent procognitive battery (SAR110894 in rat/mouse object recognition, scopolamine, Abeta25-35)
efficacy.note: Sanofi's own scientists: no sustained symptomatic efficacy in any 4-24-week AD trial despite robust rodent procognition; SAR110894 0.5-5 mg was worse than placebo on ADAS-Cog11.
efficacy.short: Three rodent successes, three AD failures
efficacy.quote: In short, duration trials (4–24 weeks) aimed at demonstrating a symptomatic effect on cognition in patients with mild or moderate AD, no real and sustained evidence of efficacy was demonstrated despite robust preclinical procognitive profile.
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC5651361). The SAR110894 trial (NCT01266525, DRI10734) has no peer-reviewed report: the result is in Sanofi's results summary (issue date 2014-11-11, tier 5, https://www.sanofi.com/assets/dotcom/content-app/clinical-studies/pharma/Letter-H/DRI10734_summary.pdf), a 2013 CTAD abstract (Stemmelin, J Nutr Health Aging 17:804-805), and an EU CTR results record (2010-022596-64, results version dated 2016-05-10 per a search snippet; the page itself returned 244 bytes to curl, so unread). ClinicalTrials.gov has no results.
efficacy.reason: Rodents procognitive; three AD trials failed
efficacy.judgement: Strengthens the 2014 contra with the class-wide, explicitly stated comparison from the SAR110894 sponsor, covering the third member. The patient numbers come from the Sanofi summary: ADAS-Cog11 estimated differences from placebo +0.26, +0.62, +0.72 (worse) at 0.5, 2, 5 mg, p=0.77/0.47/0.42, so magnitude opposite. A nominal ADCS-ADL win at 5 mg (p=0.02, unadjusted) is a secondary and changes nothing. Year is the earliest tier 1-3 date I could read; the comparison was public earlier in the tier 5 summary (2014).
efficacy.magnitude_basis: ADAS-Cog11 change vs placebo +0.26 to +0.72 (worse) at 0.5-5 mg, all non-significant (Sanofi DRI10734 summary)
efficacy.population: Unselected mild-to-moderate AD (clinical diagnosis, no biomarker selection)

patient_trials.quote: resulting in estimated difference from placebo of 0.26, 0.62, and 0.72, all statistically non-significant (nominal 2-sided p-value of respectively 0.77, 0.47, and 0.42).

efficacy.note: Six months of SAR110894 cut tau hyperphosphorylation, tangles and memory deficits in THY-Tau22 mice; no disease-modification trial was ever run, so the prediction is untested.
efficacy.quote: Long-term SAR110894 treatment could have potential disease modifying activity in neurodegenerative tauopathies.
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC5651361). No registry entry for any disease-modification trial of an H3 antagonist in AD was found.
efficacy.judgement: Separate track under the identity rule: a different model (tau transgenic, chronic 6-month dosing) making a different prediction (slowed tau pathology) from the symptomatic rodent battery. Published after the 2013 symptomatic trial failed, but it is not a retrodiction of that result, so retrodiction false; Sanofi filed a use patent (PCT/EP2013/057241) and ran no trial.
efficacy.population: Unselected mild-to-moderate AD (clinical diagnosis, no biomarker selection)

safety.model: Rat safety pharmacology and EEG, monkey toxicology (ABT-288)
safety.note: Rodent safety pharmacology claimed a wide CNS and cardiovascular margin; rat EEG put wake-promoting exposures above procognitive ones. Sanofi's rat sleep-wake EEG (Griebel 2012) is the same assay; its 2012 opener folds here.
safety.short: Wide CNS margin claimed; wake above efficacy
safety.quote: ABT-288 demonstrated a number of other favorable attributes, including good pharmacokinetics and oral bioavailability of 37 to 66%, with a wide central nervous system and cardiovascular safety margin.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level; the rat EEG wake-vs-procognition statement and the 580-fold monkey NOAEL margin are quoted from Othman 2013, which cites this paper.
safety.judgement: Opener. The abuse-liability battery (Bitner 2013, https://doi.org/10.1007/s00213-013-3027-7: no stimulant-like effects, no self-administration, no dependence) predicted low abuse potential; no human abuse study exists, so it stays unscored.
safety.population: Unselected mild-to-moderate AD (clinical diagnosis, no biomarker selection)

safety.model: Rat safety pharmacology and EEG, monkey toxicology (ABT-288)
safety.note: Insomnia and abnormal dreams were dose-limiting at 5-6 mg, above the rat-efficacious exposure, as rat EEG predicted; AEs at 1-3 mg in AD were mild.
safety.short: Sleep AEs where rat EEG predicted
safety.quote: Electroencephalogram studies in rats suggested that ABT-288 exposures (and therefore H3 receptor occupancy) required for wakefulness are higher than those required for the precognitive effects in behavioural models.
safety.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC3635600); 'H3' is set as 'H 3' and a citation bracket follows in the source. Healthy young and elderly volunteers, not patients. The matching sentence: 'The incidence and severity of insomnia observed at the intolerable doses of ABT-288 ... suggest that these doses already have high H3 receptor occupancy'.
safety.reason: Sleep AEs where rat EEG predicted
safety.judgement: On-target harm the model predicted in kind and in order (wake-promotion above procognitive exposure): same, direction_only. Counted here, not in dose, because the stated margin held (3 mg tolerated, above the rat band). Class-consistent: Grove 2014 (sleep disturbance, mostly at 10-20 ug titration), Sanofi DRI10734 summary (insomnia signal at 2-5 mg SAR110894), Delay-Goyet 2016 ('dose-dependent sleep disturbances was frequent across trials'). Not scored: the Sanofi summary's new findings for SAR110894 (dose-related depressed mood; LOCS-III lens opacities of undetermined significance) have no published model prediction I could check, and the ABT-288 schizophrenia psychosis-related AEs belong to another indication.
safety.magnitude_basis: sleep-related AEs dose-limiting at 5-6 mg vs 3 mg tolerated, against rat EEG wake exposure > procognitive exposure
safety.population: Unselected mild-to-moderate AD (clinical diagnosis, no biomarker selection)

safety.model: Rat safety pharmacology and EEG, monkey toxicology (ABT-288)
safety.note: In 291 AD patients on donepezil, sleep-initiation/maintenance disturbance was flagged as a safety signal, higher at 2-5 mg; three insomnia discontinuations at 5 mg.
safety.short: Insomnia signal the rat EEG missed
safety.quote: Signal detection methodology identify the High Level Term (HLT) “Disturbances in initiating and maintaining sleep” and the Preferred term (PT) “Muscle spasm” as safety signals.
safety.confidence_note: Sponsor results summary (tier 5, issue date 11-Nov-2014) read in full via pdftotext; no peer-reviewed report of NCT01266525 exists. The summary attributes insomnia and muscle spasm to 'possible cholinergic origin' (all patients on donepezil), but reports a trend to higher incidence at 2 and 5 mg and 3 insomnia discontinuations in the 5 mg arm. The EU CTR results record (2010-022596-64, v1 2016-05-10) is the tier 3 record; its adverse-event tables were not returned by the scrape, so arm-level insomnia counts are unverified.
safety.judgement: Paired comparison (comparison_stated false): the model side is Griebel 2012 BBR (no wake-promotion at 3-30 mg/kg), the patient side Sanofi's own summary flagging a dose-trending sleep-disturbance signal at the 2-5 mg doses whose exposures were procognitive in rodents. A predicted absence of an on-target harm that then appeared is contra, magnitude opposite. Year 2014 is the earliest public date of the patient side (rule 6); the tier 5 source carries trial_unreported true and registry_date is the later EU CTR posting. Not scored here: depressed mood and LOCS-III lens opacities (no model prediction found).
safety.magnitude_basis: rat EEG: no change in wakefulness or slow-wave sleep at 3-30 mg/kg p.o.; patients: HLT 'Disturbances in initiating and maintaining sleep' flagged as a safety signal, trend to higher incidence at 2 and 5 mg, 3 of 11 5-mg discontinuations for insomnia
safety.population: Unselected mild-to-moderate AD (clinical diagnosis, no biomarker selection)

safety.model: Rat safety pharmacology and EEG, monkey toxicology (ABT-288)
safety.note: Sanofi's own scientists, citing the SAR110894 trial among the H3 AD trials, record dose-dependent sleep disturbance as frequent across them.
safety.quote: The reporting of dose-dependent sleep disturbances was frequent across trials.
safety.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC5651361, epub 2016-11-03). The sentence is class-wide, covering refs 35-39 which include the SAR110894 phase 2 abstract (Stemmelin 2013, J Nutr Health Aging 17:804-805); the paper does not mention its own 2012 rat EEG result, so the comparison is paired, not stated. Registry date is the EU CTR results posting for 2010-022596-64.
safety.reason: Rat EEG predicted no insomnia; signal appeared
safety.judgement: Strengthens the 2014 contra with a tier 1 peer-reviewed patient-side statement from the SAR110894 sponsor; status unchanged. The class-wide wording is why confidence stays medium rather than high.
safety.magnitude_basis: rat EEG: no sleep/wake change at 3-30 mg/kg p.o.; trials: dose-dependent sleep disturbance reported as frequent (Delay-Goyet 2016), with Sanofi's DRI10734 sleep-disturbance safety signal at 2-5 mg
safety.population: Unselected mild-to-moderate AD (clinical diagnosis, no biomarker selection)
